newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's profits seen topping one bln pound mark.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's profits seen topping one bln pound mark.

text.p: Lloyd's of London profits are expected to top the billion pound mark for the second year running when it reports results for the the 1994 year of account on Friday.
The results are likely to be broadly in-line with predictions made at the time of last year's figures.
Lloyd's returned to the black 12 months ago with profits of 1.08 billion pound, after five years of record losses totalling more than eight billion pounds.
The insurance market forecast then that profits for 1994 would be around 1.008 billion pounds.
Lloyd's reports results three years in arrears.
In April, it reported preliminary 1994 profits of 1.005 billion pounds.

Those results were before tax and after members' personal expenses. They were based on an initial review of syndicate returns representing 94 percent of the market's 1994 capacity of 10.9 billion pounds and projections for the remaining syndicates.
There were 179 syndicates underwriting in 1994, which closed at year-end 1996 under Lloyd's three-year accounting system.
Projected results for the 1995 and 1996 years of account will also be published on Friday.

Speaking in Japan earlier this week, Rowland said 1996 profits were likely to fall back to around 600 to 700 million pounds in 1996 as a result of pressure on premium rates following another year of profits around the one billion pound level in 1995.
Competition in insurance markets worldwide has forced down rates over the past couple of years and is likely to continue to do so in the immediate future.
